rule.title: Diamond Sleet APT Scheduled Task Creation - Registry
rule.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

es.summary: Se creó o modificó en TaskCache\Tree una clave de registro de una tarea programada llamada "Windows TeamCity Settings User Interface". Diamond Sleet usó este nombre de tarea tras explotar la CVE-2023-42793 de TeamCity.
es.what_it_detects: Eventos de registro cuyo TargetObject contiene a la vez \SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\Schedule\TaskCache\Tree\ y el texto "Windows TeamCity Settings User Interface". Windows escribe esa clave al registrar una tarea programada con ese nombre.
es.why_it_matters: Según el informe de Microsoft citado, Diamond Sleet registró esta tarea para ejecutar su payload después de comprometer servidores TeamCity. Una tarea programada da al atacante persistencia y ejecución de código que sobreviven a reinicios. La regla está etiquetada como debilitamiento de defensas (T1685).
triage_steps: Revise el rol del host: ¿es un servidor TeamCity o un build agent? Anote la versión de TeamCity y si tiene aplicado el parche de la CVE-2023-42793.
Revise TargetObject, EventType, Details e Image. Obtenga la acción de la tarea, por ejemplo con schtasks /query /tn "Windows TeamCity Settings User Interface" /v /fo list.
Ubique el binario que ejecuta la tarea. Obtenga su hash, su firma y su fecha de creación, y consúltelos en inteligencia de amenazas.
Pivote en el mismo host +/- 15 minutos: creación de procesos schtasks.exe o powershell.exe, sobre todo si el proceso padre es Java de TeamCity.
Revise los logs web o de acceso de TeamCity: busque solicitudes no autenticadas a /RPC2 y tokens o usuarios administradores nuevos o inesperados en ese período.
Busque en toda la flota el mismo nombre de tarea, el mismo hash y los mismos destinos salientes. Revise también alertas previas de este host.
false_positives: No se esperan; la regla indica Unknown. JetBrains no instala ninguna tarea con este nombre. Trate la alerta como maliciosa hasta confirmar que se trata de una prueba autorizada de red team o de detección.
response_steps: Verifique la tarea y su payload. Luego aísle el host de la red y conserve el acceso de administración para el análisis forense.
Antes de eliminar nada, recolecte el XML de la tarea, el binario del payload, la memoria y los logs de TeamCity.
Deshabilite y elimine la tarea, borre el payload y revoque los tokens y credenciales de TeamCity que estuvieron expuestos en el servidor.
Parchee TeamCity y, si hace falta, reconstruya el servidor desde un estado confiable. Antes de volver a producción, revise si los artefactos de build fueron alterados.
es.severity_rationale: El nivel alto se justifica porque este nombre de tarea lo usó un actor conocido, es poco probable en software legítimo e indica persistencia en un servidor que puede contener código fuente y secretos.

en.summary: A registry key for a scheduled task named "Windows TeamCity Settings User Interface" was created or changed under the TaskCache\Tree hive. Diamond Sleet used this task name after exploiting TeamCity CVE-2023-42793.
en.what_it_detects: Registry events where TargetObject contains both \SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\Schedule\TaskCache\Tree\ and the string "Windows TeamCity Settings User Interface". Windows writes this key whenever a scheduled task with that name is registered.
en.why_it_matters: The referenced Microsoft report says Diamond Sleet registered this task to run its payload after compromising TeamCity servers. Scheduled tasks give attackers persistence and code execution that can survive reboots. The rule is tagged under defense impairment (T1685).
triage_steps: Check the host role: is it a TeamCity server or build agent? Note the TeamCity version and whether the CVE-2023-42793 patch was applied.
Review TargetObject, EventType, Details and Image. Find the task's action, for example with schtasks /query /tn "Windows TeamCity Settings User Interface" /v /fo list.
Locate the binary the task runs, get its hash, signer and creation time, and check it against threat intelligence.
Pivot on the same host +/- 15 minutes: process creation for schtasks.exe or powershell.exe, especially with TeamCity's Java process as the parent.
Look at TeamCity web or access logs for unauthenticated requests to /RPC2 or for new or unexpected admin tokens or users created around that time.
Search the whole fleet for the same task name, the same hash and the same outbound destinations, and check for earlier alerts on this host.
false_positives: None are expected; the rule lists Unknown. JetBrains does not ship a task by this name. Treat a hit as malicious until you can show it was an authorized red-team or detection test.
response_steps: Verify the task and its payload. Then isolate the host from the network, keeping management access for forensics.
Collect the task XML, the payload binary, memory and the TeamCity logs before you remove anything.
Disable and delete the task, remove the payload, and revoke TeamCity tokens and credentials that were exposed on the server.
Patch TeamCity, rebuild the server from a known-good state if needed, and review build artifacts for tampering before going back into service.
en.severity_rationale: High fits because this task name was used by a known threat actor, it is unlikely to appear in legitimate software, and it points to persistence on a server that may hold source code and secrets.

positive.description: Sysmon registry event (EventID 12): the Schedule service creates the TaskCache Tree key for the malicious task on a TeamCity server
Sysmon registry event (EventID 13): the Id value is set under the malicious task's Tree key

negative.description: Legitimate Windows scheduled task key under TaskCache Tree with a different name
The task name appears in a registry path outside the TaskCache Tree hive (a user settings key), so only one of the two required strings matches
